articles.title_orig: Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
articles.title_zh: Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
articles.content_orig:
We’ve expanded our eighth generation TPU portfolio with TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, marking four new TPU systems in a single year.
SVP and Chief Technologist, AI and Infrastructure
We’re expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx for secure, confidential inference and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows. These systems help you manage complex agentic workloads by providing specialized hardware for security, density, and reasoning. You can learn more about these additions and our latest software updates by watching our broadcast or visiting the Google Cloud website to explore our full infrastructure lineup.
We first designed TPUs more than a decade ago motivated by Google’s internal demands, including voice recognition and language translation. Eight generations of TPUs later, the use cases have exploded, covering: i) training and serving our own Gemini models, ii) agentic workloads, iii) delivering services to Google Cloud customers on our cloud infrastructure, and most recently, iv) allowing customers to deploy TPUs directly into their own data centers. TPUs are now a rapidly growing business with nearly 100 customers — including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers, universities, and more.
At Google Cloud Next in April, we introduced two new specialized TPUs in the same generation — 8t for large-scale training and 8i for real-time reasoning. TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better inference price performance, respectively, versus our previous generation of TPUs.
Today, we’re taking that a step further, expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two additional systems: TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack, and TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference. This is the first time we have introduced four TPU systems in a single year.
Our expanded eighth-generation TPU portfolio: TPU 8t, TPU 8i, TPU 8tx, and TPU 8i Max.
While we’ve always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we’re now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads.
The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality. Coupled with our recent PyTorch announcements , our aim is to make TPUs more easily accessible to every developer and Cloud customer. By combining modular custom silicon with an open and easy-to-use software stack, we can deliver new hardware and system configurations at the pace of the AI industry.
Today, we’re announcing two new TPU systems — and there’s an important difference between a new chip and a new system.
Designing a new chip means laying out billions of microscopic transistors on a silicon wafer in a multi-year process bound by the laws of physics and a complex, long-duration manufacturing lifecycle. A system, on the other hand, is about how we bring together the compute, networking, and storage around the chip. This can include how they are packaged with the chips, to quickly meet emerging customer needs and research use cases.
When we built our very first TPU more than a decade ago, we knew AI software would evolve much faster than silicon manufacturing ever could. So we made a foundational bet on system balance and modularity, architecting our TPUs as building blocks as part of our AI Hypercomputer , so engineers could rapidly adjust packaging, high-speed memory, optical networking, and security around them. That approach allows us to deliver specialized supercomputers in a matter of months rather than years.
Each system in our eighth-generation TPU portfolio targets a distinct part of the AI lifecycle. TPU 8t and TPU 8i established the baseline for this generation of chips:
Now, as enterprises bring autonomous agents into production, we have created two new configurations of these foundational systems to solve two urgent new challenges: hardware-level data security and million-token context scale.
TPU 8tx, our third eighth-generation system, is optimized for secure and confidential inference and is also great for small-scale training. It’s built for regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models and autonomous agents alongside their most sensitive data.
Normally, data is encrypted when stored or sent over a network, but has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. Built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, TPU 8tx builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use. And by adopting the same low-latency Boardfly network we created for real-time reasoning, TPU 8tx keeps multi-step agents moving, delivering up to 2x lower latency compared to TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty.
Pairing training-grade compute with a fast inference network also means organizations can simultaneously run and customize their models on a single system. TPU 8tx enables teams to fine-tune models using their private data, distill large models into smaller ones, and train their agents through reinforcement learning, all without needing to migrate sensitive data between separate clusters.
Designed for sensitive enterprise workloads, TPU 8tx provides hardware-level confidential compute for private fine-tuning and secure agent execution.
Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall.
When dozens of AI agents work together across an entire software codebase or hours of video at once, memory bandwidth quickly becomes the bottleneck. So we took two low-latency TPU 8i chips and combined them onto a single package.
TPU 8i Max scales compute and memory in lockstep, delivering double the compute, double the SRAM and double the HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i, so processors remain equipped with essential data and so that large workloads do not stall. Further, because TPU 8i Max fits twice the silicon within the existing rack footprint, data centers can deploy significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt.
The dual-chip TPU 8i Max system, engineered for massive context windows and maximum compute density.
While flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack.
When we launched the first TPU more than a decade ago, there were only a handful of companies running workloads that needed the processing power of a TPU. The use cases were specialized, so engineers would use optimized frameworks and hand-tuned code.
Over the years, as AI has advanced, more and more companies began using accelerators. Now, AI adoption is at a point where TPUs are excellent for a wide range of companies and use cases, and as a result, we’ve been working systematically to remove barriers to adoption so that TPUs are as easy-to-use as general-purpose hardware.
This investment comes together today across these key areas:
Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams, and Google DeepMind researchers build side-by-side.
Increasingly, we’re even tapping into AI to ideate and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. From using Google DeepMind’s AlphaChip reinforcement learning system to using Gemini to deliver chip layouts in hours rather than weeks, we’re using TPU-powered AI services to rapidly accelerate next-generation TPU hardware development. articles.title_orig: New PS Portal Announced, Future-Proofed with Internal Storage and Only for Japan
articles.title_zh: New PS Portal Announced, Future-Proofed with Internal Storage and Only for Japan
articles.content_orig:
Sony has today announced a new model of the PS Portal will be future-proofed with the addition of internal storage. The new version is launching on 10th December 2026 at the same price as the current model (¥39,980), but only in Japan.
Just like the Japan-specific PS5 console Sony sells, this new PS Portal model can only be set to the Japanese language and use a PSN account from the Japan region.
The new model also comes in black, but the big detail here is the fact Sony has "an eye towards future functionality", as it includes internal storage for the PS Portal. More information on that front is coming soon.
It doesn't share any further details on what the addition might entail, but the PS6 is rumoured to have a handheld device supporting the home console. Might that have something to do with the PS Portal refresh? This model also comes with a month of PS Plus Premium bundled in, so you can start streaming PS5 games straight away.
Since you don't need a PS5 anymore to stream your games, and can just do it via a PS Plus Premium membership, Sony is also updating this new model's name:
"Reflecting this expansion of gameplay beyond remote play, the product name for this new model has been changed from 'PlayStation Portal Remote Player' to 'PlayStation Portal Player.'"
The new PS Portal mode is available to pre-order from 13th November 2026, with a view to releasing on 10th December in Japan. We'll keep you updated on whether this updated version is announced for other territories.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla Are Sending Shockwaves Through Wall Street With This $53 Billion Warning
articles.title_zh: Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla Are Sending Shockwaves Through Wall Street With This $53 Billion Warning
articles.content_orig:
For the better part of the last four years, no catalyst has played a bigger role in lifting the broader market than the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) . Whether it's AI-accelerating hardware or AI applications, an IDC report pegs this cumulative addressable opportunity at $22.5 trillion from 2025 to 2031.
Few companies have taken the AI bull by the horns more than Nvidia ( NVDA +2.77% ) , Palantir Technologies ( PLTR +3.48% ) , and Tesla ( TSLA +4.23% ) .
Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) are the infrastructure backbone of AI-accelerated data centers. None of its competitors are particularly close to matching the compute capabilities of its multiple generations of GPUs.
Meanwhile, AI-driven software-as-a-service provider Palantir is a veritable blueprint for deploying AI applications. The company's Gotham platform assists the U.S. military with planning and overseeing missions.
Electric-vehicle maker Tesla is also an AI applications maven. AI is integral to the success of its full self-driving software and its Optimus humanoid robots.
Image source: Getty Images.
While this trio has thrived amid the AI infrastructure build-out, the individuals who know these companies best are sending all the wrong signals to Wall Street .
Though stock market analysts spend day after day studying the same industry and the companies that define it, no one understands Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla better than their respective insiders.
An " insider " is a high-ranking executive, board member, or beneficial owner of at least 10% of a company's outstanding shares who may possess nonpublic information. Anytime an insider buys or sells their company's stock, they're legally required to file Form 4 with regulators within two business days. This allows investors to track whether a company's insiders have been buying or selling.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/06/26
In the case of this powerhouse AI trio, insiders have been undeniable net sellers of their company's stock over the trailing five years:
Collectively, insiders at these companies have sold more than $52.7 billion more of their own company's stock than they've purchased since early November 2021.
There is, however, an asterisk that should accompany the above data. Since high-ranking executives and board members are often compensated in stock or options , they're required to sell some of their holdings to cover their federal and/or state tax liability. In other words, insider selling isn't automatically a bad thing -- especially if it's for tax purposes.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/06/26
What's equally unnerving, from an investment standpoint, is the relative lack of insider buying . With the exception of one sizable purchase totaling nearly $1 billion by Tesla CEO Elon Musk, insider buying has been practically nonexistent in this trio over the trailing five years:
If insiders aren't buying, historical precedent might explain why.
For more than 30 years, every game-changing innovation has navigated an early-innings bubble-bursting event. This includes the internet, 3D printing, blockchain technology, and the metaverse.
Stock market bubbles throughout history…

AI stocks now ~40% of the market. https://t.co/RxSAh09k6F
The reason these bubbles form and subsequently burst is that investors consistently overestimate the pace of optimization for game-changing technologies . While AI solutions have been welcomed with open arms, we're likely several years away from businesses optimizing these solutions to boost sales and profits. In other words, the door is wide open for a potential AI bubble-bursting event.

articles.title_orig: Restaurant chains refocus on food quality to bring back diners
articles.title_zh: Restaurant chains refocus on food quality to bring back diners
articles.content_orig:
Juicier chicken tenders. Revamped sauces. Richer and creamier Frosties.
Across the restaurant industry, chains are turning their focus back to their food in the hopes that better quality will win back diners.
Over the last two years, consumers have dined out less frequently and grown pickier about where they choose to eat, based on data from Black Box Intelligence. In that time, "value" has been the buzzword du jour for restaurant executives, who have explained to analysts and investors that the word encompasses more than menu pricing alone.
Now, industry CEOs are turning to their corporate chefs to try to beat rivals on quality and taste, as they look to expand their definition of value. Discounts and one-off promotions can lift traffic for a time, but the actual product still matters for restaurants' long-term growth, as well as franchisee profitability.
From Wendy's to Chipotle Mexican Grill , chief executives touted new or upcoming improvements to menu items on their quarterly earnings conference calls in recent weeks.
"We think the product's improved and even better," Chipotle CEO Scott Boatwright told analysts on the company's call in late October, referring to the burrito chain's brisket, which returned to menus for a limited time Thursday.
For some chains, better food is a key step in ambitious turnaround plans.
For example, "quality food at real value" is one pillar of Wendy's five-part turnaround strategy that the chain unveiled on Thursday.
"We're also rebuilding our food offerings and have begun testing improvements to quality and craveability of our core items, including thicker, crispier bacon, a richer and creamier Frosty, whole leaf lettuce on sandwiches and improved salads," Wendy's CEO Bob Wright told analysts on the call Thursday.
That same day, the company reported its seventh straight quarter of same-store sales declines and publicly rejected a $1.4 billion takeover bid led by Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners. Wendy's said the proposal did not take into account the potential value that its turnaround plan could unlock.
There is precedent to suggest that better-tasting food can contribute to higher sales.
In 2009, Domino's Pizza changed its recipe , swapping out its sauce, adding garlic to its crust and switching to shredded mozzarella with a hint of provolone. Along with blunt commercials that compared its previous crust to cardboard and old sauce to ketchup, the changes helped to spur U.S. same-store sales growth of 9.9% the following year.
Now, some of the same team that led the Domino's turnaround is copying the playbook at Burger King's U.S. restaurants.
Part of the burger chain's multiyear comeback plan has focused on revamping its core menu items. It started earlier this year with its flagship offering, the Whopper, which received a better bun and a new mayonnaise. And in September, it rolled out an overhaul of its nuggets, switching to 100% white meat, crispier breading and a more flavorful marinade. It also reformulated its sauces.
"We've tried to look at our biggest categories first," Josh Kobza, CEO of Burger King parent Restaurant Brands International , told CNBC. "We've also thought about the ones where the fixes are more straightforward and less operationally involved."
Following the changes, Whopper sales were up by a double-digit percentage in the third quarter, Kobza said on the company's earnings call in late October. And nugget sales climbed more than 35%. Burger King said its U.S. same-store sales jumped 8.4% in the quarter.
Like Domino's, Burger King is highlighting diners' past gripes with its Whoppers and nuggets in its ads , which star Burger King U.S. president and former Domino's executive Tom Curtis.
Better-tasting food isn't just for chains that are in trouble.
Even Chili's, which has seen its same-store sales soar 52% over the past three years, is improving more of its existing menu options. After tackling its baby back ribs, burgers and nachos, it will turn next to salads and steaks, Brinker International CEO Kevin Hochman told CNBC.
"We're going to be doing more dry aging of our beef to make it more tender, versus doing it in a plant," he said. "It's a little bit more expensive, but we think the taste is going to be a whole lot better."
Chili's rival Applebee's launched a juicier chicken tender during its latest quarter, according to John Peyton, CEO of the chain's parent company Dine Brands . In 2027, Applebee's plans to overhaul more of its protein options.
"We think proteins are, number one, our biggest opportunity," Peyton told CNBC. "Number two, they're a big focus of the way people are thinking about eating right now, leaning into proteins and a little bit less with the carbs."
Chicken is also a focus for McDonald's , which is testing hand-breaded wings, strips and a sandwich in a handful of Chicago-area restaurants. It plans to expand the trial to more locations in the U.S. and Ireland in early 2027.
Moreover, McDonald's is trying to improve its coffee, with fresher beans and upgraded equipment, executives said at the company's investor day in September. Both chicken and coffee are fast-growing categories, offering more opportunities to lift sales than McDonald's signature beef burgers.
While the burger giant isn't in full turnaround mode like rivals Wendy's and Burger King, its U.S. business has struggled in recent quarters after its value strategy didn't gain the traction the company had hoped. In the third quarter, its U.S. same-store sales fell 0.2%.
In addition to menu tests, McDonald's is also leaning into training to improve the quality and consistency of its core menu items. Starting in October, the company launched "Make It Golden," a multiyear training program for corporate employees, restaurant workers and franchisees.
Ultimately, improved menu items mean little if the recipe changes aren't well executed.

articles.title_orig: New climate reality outruns the old COP agenda
articles.title_zh: New climate reality outruns the old COP agenda
articles.content_orig:
Host countries Turkey and Australia on Monday called for more pace and determination in combating climate change at the opening of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, as experts warned that 2027 could be the warmest year on record.
Turkish Environment Minister and summit president Murat Kurum told delegates, according to a manuscript of his speech, that "delay carries one of the heaviest costs in climate action."
"Postpone an investment in resilience today, and tomorrow we may face the cost of a disaster. Fail to deliver adaptation finance today, and tomorrow's humanitarian crisis may be worse," he said.
"A drought in one part of the world is felt at the dinner table in another."
The official opening was initially delayed, partly because of discussions over the conference's agenda.
Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen acknowledged that the 1.5-degrees-Celcius target set out in the Paris Agreement would likely not be met.
"The latest science tells us that we will overshoot 1.5. But we can still return if we work together and act with urgency, solidarity and resolve," he said.
"Paris is working, but we must move faster," he said. "We have the tools. The technologies we need are proven, commercial and scalable. What we need is to speed up deployment," he urged.
UN climate chief Simon Stiell in his opening speech warned that "progress is nowhere near fast or fair enough." While no single conference could be a "silver bullet," this one must bring progress, he said.
Specifically, Stiell called for measures to electrify and to cut methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas.
"Together, action on methane and electrification are a planetary icepack - able to cut half a degree from projected global heating," he said.
Turkey and Australia are co-hosts of the climate conference this year. Turkey is hosting the meeting and holds the presidency through Environment Minister Kurum. Australian Climate Minister Bowen serves as "president of the negotiations" and is to explore the lines of compromise.
The talks began as the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) released its latest State of the Climate report.
The report said that the year 2027 could be the hottest on record, with a strong El Niño expected to bring further extreme heat.
El Niño acts as a "risk multiplier," WMO Secretary General Celeste Saulo said in Geneva. "Heatwaves, tropical cyclones, and rainstorms are intensifying faster than our historical baselines prepared us for."
The past four years, 2023-2026, are the four warmest years on record, the report said. Global mean sea level meanwhile reached a record high in 2026.
"We have entered a new age of climate extremes," said UN Secretary General António Guterres in the report. "A supersized El Niño is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change. Climate records keep falling. The human costs keep rising. And those least responsible are suffering first and worst," he said.
Civil society organizations, in a joint letter to the COP31 presidency, urged the conference to "focus on keeping alive the goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C - a survival line for communities, ecosystems and economies."
COP31 "must serve to rebuild trust in the multilateral process," the letter said.
Environmental organizations called for an organized exit from using fossil fuels: coal, oil and gas.
Two years ago, it was agreed that industrialized nations would provide at least $300 billion annually in climate finance by 2035 at the latest. The money is intended to help countries adapt to new extreme conditions and also to reduce their own emissions.

articles.title_orig: Chinese zero tariff rule boosts South African apples
articles.title_zh: Chinese zero tariff rule boosts South African apples
articles.content_orig:
By Fred Meintjes 2026-11-09T11:11:00+00:00
Tru-Cape says China’s new tariff deal for Africa is already benefitting South African exporters
The South African fruit business has said that while it has been able to grow exports to China under the country’s zero tariff deal for African countries, there is a short window of opportunity for it to negotiate a permanent trade deal.
The country’s apple exporters revealed this week that they have seen a significant increase in shipments to China.
“The removal of Chinese import tariffs on South African fruit is already delivering results for Tru-Cape Fruit Marketing, with the company’s apple exports to China increasing by almost 50 per cent year-to-date,” stated Tru-Cape Marketing.
”The development has created new opportunities to grow South African apples’ presence in one of the world’s largest consumer markets, while highlighting the need for more competitive market access in India.”
Previously, South African fruit entering China was subject to a 10 per cent import tariff.
The reduction to 0 per cent has levelled the playing field for Southern Hemisphere suppliers, giving South African exporters a more competitive position in the market.
This is likely to also provide further impetus for South African pear, table grape, stonefruit and citrus exporters.
“It is important that we secure a longer-term free trade agreements deal,” the Citrus Growers Association recently commented.
“The playing field is now definitely level, with all Southern Hemisphere countries enjoying a zero tariff,” noted Conrad Fick, marketing director at Tru-Cape.
Tru-Cape currently accounts for more than 20 per cent of South African apple exports to the market.
”South African Royal Gala Red and Royal Beaut apples are performing particularly well, and we are also seeing growing acceptance of the Flash Gala brand, which is helping to increase both volumes and prices,” said Fick.
The country’s stonefruit exporters are also looking forward to their first season in the Chinese market.
“We are particularly excited about building with Sugar Prunes which is already well accepted amongst Chinese consumers,” added Luhan Marais of Icon Fruit.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Board to Probe Spying Case After CEO Admits Affair
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Board to Probe Spying Case After CEO Admits Affair
articles.content_orig:
The chief executive of one of the world's largest public corporations is facing an inquiry following reports he conducted an 'affair' with an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang serves as chief executive officer of Nvidia, presently ranked second only to Apple amongst the globe's largest publicly traded firms, and is reported to have acknowledged the affair.
The $4.5 trillion American technology giant initiated the independent inquiry after reports emerged that its founder and CEO had become the subject of a 'foreign intelligence effort', the Nvidia Board of Directors confirmed in a statement.
The New York Times referenced US intelligence officials who identified businesswoman Alice Huang as a suspected Chinese operative.
Jensen Huang has now acknowledged he was "unfaithful" to his wife and expressed remorse for the pain he has inflicted upon her and their children, according to subsequent reports.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's Board stated it possessed no grounds to suspect that company secrets or US national security had been jeopardised - and indicated Mr Huang remained committed to continuing his leadership of the business.
Nvidia ranks amongst the world's most valuable corporations and is regarded as pivotal to manufacturing the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with Mr Huang having led it for over three decades.
The announcement followed Mr Huang's admission to the board that he had been intimate with a Chinese business executive, whom US intelligence identified as collecting information for Beijing, The New York Times reported. Mr Huang issued an apology in a message to the firm, the Times reported.
"I was unfaithful to my wife," he said.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Nvidia's board stated it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but confirmed its investigation would scrutinise all available evidence.
Mr Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to co-operating with it," the board said.
Mr Huang, 63, will continue as chief executive throughout the probe.
The Times disclosed last month that US intelligence services had uncovered that Mr Huang had formed a close association with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and chip purchaser, and concluded that she was passing intelligence straight to Beijing.
The pair are not related, the Times confirmed.
Alice Huang previously worked as a television journalist in China before rising to senior executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed, which has emerged as one of Nvidia's largest clients in Southeast Asia.
Megaspeed purchased more than 4.8 billion US dollars (£3.6 billion) worth of Nvidia chips during the past two years, the Times reported.
In a statement issued in recent hours, the Nvidia Board announced: "The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.
"Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.
"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk axes the Cybertruck and says buyers will get refunds
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk axes the Cybertruck and says buyers will get refunds
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
The Cybertruck will cease production next year, with the wind-down slated for mid-2027 at Tesla 's facility outside Austin , Texas .
Elon Musk announced the model's demise on Friday in a curt post on X, his social media site, noting that production of the vehicle “will be winding down” around mid-2027.
Musk said the move was to allow increased production of the Cybercab robotaxi, a vehicle central to the automaker's autonomous-driving ambitions. The Tesla CEO has also said the company will add an extra production shift to fulfill outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the production line next year.
Musk said many customers who put down deposits for the pickup will have to be refunded, as orders far exceed production capacity. "We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people," the billionaire said in a post on X on Monday.
For the Cybertruck, a pet project of Musk who insisted it was Tesla's best product, it marks an unceremonious end to one of the auto industry's most ballyhooed debuts.
“Few vehicles in history have generated as much attention,” said Armen Hareyan, whose Torque News site covers autos. “The Cybertruck became a cultural symbol – loved, mocked and impossible to ignore.”
The truck rolled onto the scene in a dramatic unveiling in 2019, when a Tesla designer hurled a metal ball at the vehicle to demonstrate its supposedly unbreakable glass, only to see it shatter. He repeated the stunt on another window of the truck, shattering that one, too. Even as some critics scoffed, Musk was steadfast.
“I just wanted to make a futuristic battle tank — something that looks like it could come out of ‘Blade Runner’ or ‘ Aliens ’ or something like that but was also highly functional,” he told Automotive News.
He called it “a better sports car than a Porsche 911” and “a better truck than an F-150.” It struck some as the perfect vehicular reflection of the brash, convention-busting Musk.
“A really controversial vehicle unveiled by a controversial individual into a market where none of the electric trucks have been able to really capture demand,” said Spencer Penn, a former Tesla executive who left the company before the Cybertruck's launch and now heads software developer LightSource.
Penn remembered watching the unveiling and feeling initially revolted by the sight of the Cybertruck, calling its appearance “madness.” But the more he looked at it, the more his opinion changed. He signed up for a pre-sale reservation, though ended up not getting a Cybertruck when Musk's promises of a price tag under $40,000 went unmet and the first trucks sold for double or more.
Penn called the Cybertruck part of Tesla's adventurous spirit that drives innovation. “Some of these bets work and some of these bets don’t,” he said. Tesla began delivering the Cybertruck in late 2023, but demand has fallen far short of Musk's expectations.
Musk once forecast he'd make 250,000 Cybertrucks a year. U.S. sales fell 48% to 20,237 units last year, according to Kelley Blue Book, well below Musk's earlier projection that annual Cybertruck sales could reach 250,000 vehicles. Sales through the end of September this year were down another 28%, according to Kelley Blue Book.
While the decision to end Cybertruck production may be driven by sales realities, it also reflects Tesla's shift to autonomous vehicles, on which Musk is betting the company's future. If the imposing, sharp-angled, dystopian appearance of the Cybertruck weren't enough to turn many potential buyers away, Musk did so himself by allying with a panoply of right-wing figures, most notably President Donald Trump .
He alienated some customers as his image morphed from eccentric innovator to polarizing force, trading his billions for political influence. Once-passionate Tesla drivers rushed to sell off their cars, or slapped stickers on the bumper declaring, “I bought this before Elon went crazy.” Organizers staged demonstrations outside Tesla showrooms and urged investors to dump shares of the company's stock.
Anger spilled into violence, with Molotov cocktails hurled at Tesla vehicles, charging stations set ablaze, and dealerships covered in graffiti. Lovers of the Cybertruck became targets, too, subjected to shouts of “ Nazi !” and extended middle fingers. Ross Blankenship is one of them.
When he first laid eyes on the Cybertruck, he felt transported back to his childhood, when he played “Halo,” the sci-fi video game. He had to have it. “I had that sort of child in me wanting to be part of something cool that would change the future of automotive,” Blankenship said in a call from his Cybertruck as he drove through Sunnyside, Colorado .
Even though Blankenship agreed with Musk on politics, he hated seeing a vehicle he loved turned into a political symbol. “I never bought it for any other reason than the fascination with the future technology of trucks … so that was a little heartbreaking.” He would buy another Cybertruck again in a heartbeat, calling its end “a sad moment.” The stainless-steel pickup, which inspired devotion and derision with its science-fiction looks, will stop rolling off the line in Texas next year.

articles.title_orig: Rubio sees little hope of diplomatic breakthrough to Mideast deadlock amid 'outrageous' Iranian demands
articles.title_zh: Rubio sees little hope of diplomatic breakthrough to Mideast deadlock amid 'outrageous' Iranian demands
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Iran of "outrageous and ridiculous" demands as efforts to reach a lasting resolution in the Middle East war appeared stalled.
Speaking with reporters in Florida on Sunday evening before traveling to Paris for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting, Rubio indicated the two sides remain far apart on negotiations, after Tehran proposed shortening the timetable for restarting talks from seven days to two.
Rubio said President Donald Trump would prefer to solve "this and every problem diplomatically," but added that "sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately."
Energy prices moved lower on Monday morning after President Trump said Sunday that further strikes were "highly unlikely" if negotiations progressed toward a strong agreement.
Brent crude , the international price benchmark, was down 0.75% at $97.58 per barrel by 5:25 a.m. ET. Meanwhile, U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery were trading 0.42% lower at $90.45.
Trump said in a CNN interview prior to Rubio's comments that a resumption of hostilities in the more than eight-month-long conflict was unlikely, provided that talks to constrain Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz can progress.
"I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said. "Right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable but, in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic."
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday that Tehran wants U.S. sanctions lifted and the war ended on all fronts before negotiations begin.

articles.title_orig: Gears of War: E-Day celebrates franchise's 20th Anniversary with free Raam skin
articles.title_zh: Gears of War: E-Day celebrates franchise's 20th Anniversary with free Raam skin
articles.content_orig:
Gears of War: E-Day is bringing back Guardian for a two-week anniversary event, as the series celebrates 20 years. Players also get a new Horde Siege variant before Season 2: Legacy arrives on December 1.
The Coalition also announced a RAAM multiplayer character as a free anniversary gift for E-Day players, with claims starting November 7, the anniversary of the original game’s release.
There is one distinction for anyone picking up the news late: the character is free for E-Day players, not a free copy of the game. The studio’s announcement does not give a claim deadline, so check the game for current availability.
Image: The Coalition / Xbox Game Studios
RAAM was the original Gears of War’s formidable Locust general, and his return gives players another character for E-Day multiplayer. In its anniversary announcement , The Coalition said players could claim the gift instantly by logging in starting November 7. It did not specify an end date, so check the game for current availability.
Image: The Coalition / Xbox Game Studios
The free character is separate from the anniversary playlists. Guardian puts leaders at the center of a Versus match, while For the Queen changes Horde Siege by disabling the supply cache. Squads must rely on their loadouts rather than using that cache.
The developer describes the event as lasting two weeks, but the announcement does not specify an exact end time. The in-game playlists are the place to check which modes are available when you play.
Image: The Coalition / Xbox Game Studios
The Coalition says Season 2: Legacy begins December 1 and will revisit 20 years of Gears through maps, modes and multiplayer skins. It has shown one character look: Solemn Memories Dom, based on the suit Dominic Santiago wears in his photograph with Maria in Gears of War 2.
The announcement does not list every returning map or explain how each Season 2 cosmetic will be obtained. For PC players, E-Day is available on Steam for Windows ; it is also available on Xbox. Online play requirements and access can vary by platform.

articles.title_orig: Dulles Airport to unveil new concourse with 14 gates, restaurants and passenger lounge
articles.title_zh: Dulles Airport to unveil new concourse with 14 gates, restaurants and passenger lounge
articles.content_orig:
Dulles International Airport is preparing to open a new concourse featuring additional gates, restaurants and passenger amenities, three years after construction began.
Reporters will get a first look at Concourse E on Monday when the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority hosts a grand opening ceremony. While the event is not open to the public, an MWAA spokesperson told WTOP that more details about the concourse’s opening date will be announced soon.
Concourse E will provide additional space for airlines and travelers as the airport experiences record passenger growth, the airports authority said .
The 435,000-square-foot facility will feature 14 gates, expanded seating areas, upgraded restrooms and direct access to the airport’s AeroTrain system.
The concourse will also include 44,000 square feet of dining and retail space, featuring Dos Toros Taqueria, Good Company Doughnuts & Café, Bonchon and Honor Brewing.
Additional amenities include a 40,000-square-foot lounge for United Airlines passengers, duty-free shopping and a video gaming lounge.
Airport officials said the expansion is needed as passenger growth puts pressure on existing gates, particularly those used by United Airlines.
“United’s A, C and D-gate waiting areas need more room for connecting passengers. Additional stores and restaurants are needed to service passengers, especially at peak arrival and departure times,” the airports authority said.
Construction on the concourse, a joint project between the airports authority and United Airlines, began in November 2023.
“Having a facility with 14 more international capable gates is going to let us double the international service out of here,” United CEO Scott Kirby said in December 2024.
Concourse E is part of the Global Gateway IAD modernization program and the first of four planned construction phases. The program is expected to invest more than $20 billion in airport improvements.
WTOP’s Neal Augenstein contributed to this report from Dulles International Airport.

articles.title_orig: He fought France's far right for half a century. Now Mélenchon's presidential bid may hand it power
articles.title_zh: He fought France's far right for half a century. Now Mélenchon's presidential bid may hand it power
articles.content_orig:
Jean-Luc Melenchon has been described as a “radical” by right-wing opponents, a “despot” by former allies and a “hero” by some of the students who have taken to the streets in nationwide protests .
The leader of the France Unbowed (LFI) party has emerged as the strongest contender on the left and potential challenger to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen in next year’s presidential election.
On Saturday, Melenchon is presenting his programme at a rally in Le Bourget, north of Paris, a day after it was published online. Among his proposals, he wants to lower the retirement age to 60 and raise the minimum wage to 1,700 euro ($1,900) a month; pull France out of NATO and renationalise parts of the economy.
He wants France to stop paying back the debt it owes to the European Central Bank, effectively transforming it into a permanent interest-free loan – a move he hopes would give the government more room to spend.
On Europe, he envisions France remaining in the EU, but he wants to refuse rules that conflict with the nation’s social, environmental or economic programmes, setting up a potentially confrontational relationship with Brussels.
His party is gaining momentum as protests led by students in mid-September swelled to include several groups angry about failing public services, rising living costs and uncertain futures. He has been hailed at marches, some of which have seen vandalism and looting.
“His strength is that he is in tune with the demands of the demonstrations: better wages, money in education, a lot of welfare measures, no austerity cuts which appease people who are fed up with the cost of living,” said Jacques Reland, a senior research fellow at the Global Policy Institute. “He is the vote of the protesters.”
But some say his policies are radical and unrealistic.
France’s finances and borrowing are under scrutiny as its budget deficit and debt levels are high, raising further doubts on how Melenchon’s ambitious spending plans, particularly on social programmes and public investment, could be implemented. Some economists warn that his plans could cause investors to sell French government bonds, thereby increasing sovereign borrowing cost. “Borrowing money and deciding not to give it back – that’s called theft,” Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said in September, regarding such proposals.
LFI says higher taxes on wealthy individuals and corporations – another pillar of Melenchon’s campaign – would finance its spending plans. His proposals include a minimum 2 percent tax on the wealth of billionaires, restoring France’s wealth tax and increasing taxes on large inheritances. “Financial capital has benefitted, and it is the one that should pay,” he said in October.
His programme draws on a tradition of left-wing economic interventionism, rooted partly in Keynesian thought, that argues that the state should play an active role in the economy to correct market’s imbalances.
“Because this tradition of state intervention in economic and social affairs has been abandoned by most other political parties, the fact that LFI continues to define itself through such interventionism creates an impression of radicalism,” said political analyst Beligh Nabli, a professor of public law at UPEC-Paris XII. “Yet, this radicalism is only relative – it appears radical when compared to other contemporary political offerings, but from the perspective of the history of social democracy, it is not radical at all.”
Melenchon, 75, was born in Morocco to French parents. He moved to France as a child where he later graduated in philosophy and modern literature. In the 1980s, he joined the Socialist Party, but distanced himself from it when it shifted towards more liberal economics.
In 2008, he finally quit the Socialists and founded the Left Party, which would later evolve into LFI. The party appealed to working-class voters and marginalised communities and became popular with young people. According to this week’s polls, the presidential candidate is polling between 17.5 to 18 percent, widening the gap with his rivals in the left camp.
Trailing behind is Raphael Glucksmann, who leads the centre-left Place Publique party and secured the backing of the Socialist Party after winning a joint primary in October. Further back, and running on their own ticket – the Communist Party’s Fabien Roussel, Marine Tondelier’s Greens party and independent Francois Ruffin.
The left-wing bloc is undecided on the LFI. As Melenchon holds a significant lead, smaller parties are weighing whether to support him to give a left-wing alliance a better shot. Glucksmann has ruled that out, but others are pondering the situation. “This will be one of the key debates throughout the presidential campaign,” said Nabil.
Another source of tension across the French left is Melenchon’s strong support of Palestine. He has repeatedly refused to describe Hamas as a “terrorist organisation” and has accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza – a term other left-wing politicians, including Glucksmann, have been reluctant to use. Melenchon has also faced accusations from political opponents on the left that his rhetoric fuels anti-Semitism, claims he rejects.
But Melenchon’s popularity is nowhere close to that of National Rally candidate Marine Le Pen. The far-right leader, who challenged President Emmanuel Macron in a second round in the past two elections, would easily win in a run-off against Melenchon, leading 70 percent to 30 percent, according to a Toluna Harris Interactive poll conducted in October.
Analysts say his economic programme is not the only obstacle. His combative political style and reputation for confrontation over compromise hinder his chances of broadening support beyond a core base.
“In France, it is often said that to win a presidential election, one must campaign from the centre. Yet, the defining characteristic of the LFI programme is that it is not centrist – that is precisely what makes it disruptive. He seeks victory, but not a victory from the centre,” Nabli said.
His leadership has also been criticised.
Several former allies have said their break with the party was driven by both Melenchon’s management style and political disagreements. Former LFI candidate Thomas Guenole has described the movement as a “dictatorship” governed by “an autocrat”, while former lawmaker Raquel Garrido said there was a left that agreed with LFI’s programme but not with the party leader’s “methods”. Former close ally Clementine Autain has likewise accused LFI of becoming “authoritarian”.
“He is the ‘supreme leader’,” said Reland at the Global Policy Institute. “The party is very organised, but it’s not a democratic party at all.”

articles.title_orig: Sony revives classic Walkman headphones as MDR-3R
articles.title_zh: Sony revives classic Walkman headphones as MDR-3R
articles.content_orig:
Sony’s MDR-3R is a modern remake of the 1979 MDR-3, the headphones that debuted alongside the very first Walkman
The silver on-ear set reproduces the original’s headband bend, perforated sound holes and “Dynamic Stereo Headphones” marking down to the vintage-style packaging
A plug-in USB-C connection, in-line remote and built-in mic replace batteries and Bluetooth pairing entirely
Sony is reissuing one of the most important headphones in its catalog with the MDR-3R, a reworked version of the MDR-3 that shipped with the original Walkman in 1979. The silver pair keeps the lightweight, open-air formula that made portable listening possible in the first place, then rewires it for modern phones, tablets and laptops through a direct USB-C plug.
To understand why the MDR-3R matters, you have to go back to the cassette era. Sony’s first Walkman , the TPS-L2, arrived with the MDR-3 as its companion, and together the two turned music into something people could carry through the city rather than leave at home on a stereo. The original Walkman launched in Japan in July 1979 and famously featured two headphone jacks so a pair of listeners could share a tape. At a time when most headphones were heavy, studio-style cans, the MDR-3’s featherweight build helped make the whole concept wearable.
Sony has treated the reissue with collector-level care. The SONY logo and “Dynamic Stereo Headphones” lettering are precision-finished to match the 1979 model, and the distinctive headband curve and perforated sound holes return unchanged. The rolled side arms from the original are back as well, though here they serve a practical purpose, fine-tuning how the earpads sit against the ear for a more comfortable fit. Even the box and instruction manual adopt the vintage graphic style, and the individual packaging is plastic-free.
The earpads are the most playful nod to the past. Both the blue and orange cushions associated with the classic MDR-3 come in the box, and swapping between them takes seconds, so the same pair can shift from muted to loud depending on the outfit. Sony has also kept the frame remarkably light, with the headphones weighing roughly 38g without the cable, making the MDR-3R the brand’s lightest over-head model. The understated silver build works just as well slung around the neck as it does on the ears.
Inside, 23mm drivers and an open-air structure carry over the spirit of the original’s sound while updating it for current listening habits. Sony has tuned the MDR-3R for natural vocals and a balanced profile, adding deeper bass and more extended highs without leaning on heavy processing. The open-back design also gives the compact on-ear form a wider, airier soundstage than its size suggests.
Connectivity is where the MDR-3R fully leaves 1979 behind. A 1.2m Y-type cable ends in a USB-C plug that works directly with current smartphones, tablets and PCs, so there is nothing to charge and no pairing to manage. An in-line remote handles play, pause, track skipping and volume, while an integrated microphone covers hands-free calls, online meetings and voice assistant requests. The serrated cable is designed to resist tangles in a bag. One amusing caveat: despite the heritage, Sony does not recommend plugging the MDR-3R into Walkman devices.
The Sony MDR-3R in silver is available now via Sony .

articles.title_orig: EXPLAINER - Why is the world’s top chipmaker caught in a US-China spy row?
articles.title_zh: EXPLAINER - Why is the world’s top chipmaker caught in a US-China spy row?
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing questions over allegations that a Chinese businesswoman with whom he had a romantic relationship was gathering intelligence for Beijing.
Huang – who cofounded Nvidia, the world’s second-most valuable company after Apple, more than three decades ago – admitted on Sunday to being unfaithful to his wife, but the company said it has no reason to believe United States national security or confidential information has been compromised.
Nevertheless, Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation into whether the 63-year-old Taiwan-US dual national had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation after media reports linking him to Alice Huang, a former executive at a Singapore-based data centre company.
“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” it said in a statement , adding that Jensen Huang fully backs the review.
After the revelations, Nvidia – whose market capitalisation of $4.5 trillion is higher than the gross domestic product (GDP) of Japan, the world’s fourth-largest economy – saw its stock price tumble by more than 4 percent in trading overnight into Monday.
The controversy erupted as Washington seeks to prevent China from obtaining advanced American semiconductors, including Nvidia’s most powerful artificial intelligence chips, as the US and China fiercely compete for AI supremacy.
So what do we know about the affair, and how will this impact US-China relations and the race for AI dominance?
The allegations first emerged in a New York Times investigation late last month, which reported that US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang had been recruited by Beijing to gather information about Nvidia’s chief executive and potentially influence the company’s chip sales to China.
However, the precise nature of the information she allegedly obtained, whether any sensitive material was passed to Beijing and how much Jensen Huang knew about the alleged operation remain unclear. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are not related despite sharing a last name.
The two were reportedly seen together at industry events, including a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang in Taipei during the Computex technology exhibition in 2025.
On Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged his infidelity in a staff memo.
“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said.
However, in late October, Jensen Huang had told Bloomberg News that his interactions with Alice Huang were related to her company, Megaspeed, describing them as “completely normal and not unusual”.
Also known as Huang Le, Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen and former senior executive at Megaspeed International, which provides computing infrastructure used to operate and train AI systems.
According to The New York Times, Megaspeed had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing about $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.
A profile of Alice Huang found in a Chinese investment database listed previous employment at HSBC and Chinese television broadcasters CCTV and Hunan TV, according to the AFP news agency, which said it could not independently verify those details.
Alice Huang has not publicly responded to the espionage allegations, and her whereabouts are currently unknown.
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation overseen by a committee of directors and external legal counsel to determine whether its president and CEO was targeted by foreign intelligence.
The company said it had no reason to believe national security or its proprietary information had been compromised while expressing confidence in Jensen Huang’s leadership.
“The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate,” it said, adding that Jensen Huang has pledged to cooperate with the investigation and continue leading the company.
However, the allegations have unsettled investors.
“It deals a blow to the cult of Huang that has taken over the chip world in recent years,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at Britain’s IG Group, a leading derivatives trading firm, told Al Jazeera, while adding that it was too early to determine whether this moment might prove a “major turning point” for Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
“If this turns into a broader congressional investigation, then the shares are likely to come under pressure,” Beauchamp added. “As we learned from the financial crisis [in 2008 and 2009], once you go looking for skeletons in a cupboard, you usually find them.”
Jensen Huang’s daughter, Madison, who also works at Nvidia, cancelled a planned visit to South Korea for an Nvidia AI event amid the controversy.
US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over suspicions that the company helped China obtain advanced Nvidia chips in violation of US export restrictions.
However, no criminal charges against Jensen Huang or Alice Huang have been reported. The controversy has prompted bipartisan pressure in Washington.
Republican lawmakers on Wednesday called on Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on November 18, arguing that the allegations raise serious questions about China’s potential access to sensitive US technology.
“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republican Congressmen John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.
Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren has also demanded answers from Nvidia and called for stronger legislation to prevent advanced US technology from reaching China.
“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China,” she said in a statement.
President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has defended Jensen Huang, describing him as an “honourable guy”.
Asked whether he should have acted after reportedly receiving an intelligence briefing about the allegations, Trump said, “No, I don’t think so.”
Meanwhile, ⁠⁠⁠⁠Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson ⁠⁠⁠⁠Guo Jiakun on Monday said the “so-called ⁠⁠⁠⁠Chinese spy ⁠⁠⁠⁠narrative” was unsubstantiated. “It is nothing but smears against China,” Guo added.
Jensen Huang, who is seen as a close adviser to Trump on the AI trade , has repeatedly pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China.
The scandal threatens to intensify tensions between Washington and Beijing over access to the powerful semiconductors needed to develop advanced AI systems. Semiconductors are needed to run nearly all electronics from smartphones to cars and military equipment.
Nvidia is a central player in that competition, supplying chips used by major US technology companies to train and operate AI models. It was until October 30 the most valuable company in the world.
“AI is now a technology that is really shaping national economies and GDPs, and safeguarding becomes even more serious. So protecting not only confidential secrets but also advancements for geopolitical reasons becomes even more important,” Fazl Barez, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford specialising in AI safety and governance, told Al Jazeera.
Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China over national security concerns. Nvidia’s top-of-the-line Blackwell GPU chips are banned for export to China.
The US has also clarified that restrictions apply to Chinese-owned companies operating outside China amid concerns that overseas subsidiaries could provide a route around export controls.
However, in December, Trump said Nvidia could sell its H200 chip to China, marking a major easing of US export restrictions. The H200, while not Nvidia’s top chip, is roughly six times more powerful than the model previously approved for sale to China, the H20.

articles.title_zh: Mario's Next 'Adults Welcome' LEGO Set Is "Hatching Soon"
articles.content_orig:
Nintendo and LEGO have teased the next entry in their 'Adults Welcome' Mario range, which will see Yoshi step into the limelight.
While we haven't seen the full set just yet, a new post on the Nintendo Today! app shows everything we need to know. We can see a close-up of the dino's eyes and snout in brick form, accompanied by the message, "Hatching soon".
Whether the set ends up being anything more than just Yoshi remains to be seen (we got that Super Mario World-inspired one a few years back, with a pixel art Mario in tow, let's not forget), but more Mario big builds are always a good thing.
The other sworded issue will be the price. The previous '18+' builds have come with a rather hefty price tag (the Mario and Luigi Kart sets will set you back £149.99 / £159.99 respectively), so we'd be surprised if the upcoming Yoshi isn't more of the same.
We'll be keeping an eye out for more price details and the all-important release date over the coming weeks.

articles.title_orig: US Stocks Rise as Oil Drop Outweighs Nvidia Woes: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: US Stocks Rise as Oil Drop Outweighs Nvidia Woes: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Stock futures were higher early on Monday, with traders keeping a close eye on technology shares after last week's volatility, while awaiting the release of key inflation data and earnings from major AI companies this week.
S&P 500 futures rose 0.34%, while Nasdaq 100 futures were around 0.5% higher. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average led gains, adding 0.76%.
Friday's market partially rebounded from Thursday's brutal AI-driven selloff, as chip stocks recovered on renewed buying. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite bounced 1.09% to 24,579.42 and the broad-market S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86. The blue-chip Dow , however, lost 237.33 points, or 0.46%, to settle at 51,285.73.
Broader investor sentiment remained cautious following a batch of stronger-than-expected jobs data. Additionally, concerns linger after the Democrats' strong midterm results, amid fears that tighter regulations on data center construction, energy use, and development costs could slow the AI infrastructure boom.
The tech sector will also be focused on the bombshell announcement Sunday that Nvidia's board of directors is opening an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. A proxy for Nvidia shares was lower by 2% over the last 24 hours in trading on Hyperliquid.
Liz Ann Sonders, Schwab Center for Financial Research chief investment strategist, noted that the Nasdaq and Nasdaq-100 are oversold, with heavy de-risking by traders. Thursday marked the biggest day of retail selling since the Covid pandemic, according to Vanda Research. Retail traders haven't been taking advantage of the selloff, Sonders said.
"Retail has not proven to be the dip buyers that they have been in the past," she told CNBC's "Fast Money" on Friday. "You saw a really heavy amount of net selling … we may not fully be washed out yet, but we'll have to see whether that retail trader at some point decides to step back in."
Sonders suggested that the next short-term focus should be on companies' adjustments to capex plans and expectations for future profit margins.
This week , investors are looking ahead to key AI-related earnings — CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials are all on deck — as they assess the outlook for tech and whether the recent selloff has further to run.
They'll also watch for the releases of both the consumer price index on Tuesday and the producer price index on Friday, looking for clues on the Fed's next move.
On Monday, traders will get September wholesale inventories data at 10 a.m. ET. Take-Two Interactive Software, Occidental Petroleum, KKR, Constellation Energy and Skydance are scheduled to report quarterly earnings.
Over in Asia, markets were mostly up on Monday, with Taiwanese equities leading the rise. The Taiwan Weighted Index closed 4.94% up at 41,664.7, marking the largest one-day gain since 31 July.
The index was powered by gains in tech heavyweights Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Hon Hai Precision Industry — also known as Foxconn.
Investors in Asia are also assessing October inflation data out from China, with the producer price index hitting its highest in over four years at 5.7%, and consumer inflation coming in slower than expected at 0.7%.
Nvidia shares were down around 5% in premarket trading Monday after the tech giant launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.
The key question for investors will be whether Huang will remain as CEO, according to Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.
"This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons," Ives said in a Sunday note.
European stocks got off to a mixed start on Monday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index opening lower before moving to a 0.4% gain by 8:20 a.m. in London.
Mining stocks popped 1.7% as gold and copper prices bounced back from last week's downturn.
Italian bank Unicredit was the top performer, up 4.7% after its third-quarter net profit rose by a record 24% year-on-year and as it prepares to take control of Germany's Commerzbank .
Luxury shares suffered, with LVMH , Moncler , Hermes , Kering , Burberry , Richemont and Christian Dior all trading slightly lower, as investors remained in risk-off mode and data showed mounting domestic inflation pressures in major market China.
Construction firm Hochtief fell 5.3% after Spanish group ACS said it had not considered a tender offer for shares in the company, which is its German subsidiary. Bloomberg had reported ACS was considering buying the remaining Hochtief shares it does not own or a potential merger of the firms.
Nvidia 's Frankfurt-traded shares were more than 6% lower in early European trading, as the company is rocked by an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang 's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy .
Asia-Pacific markets closed in broadly positive territory on Monday, amid a tech rebound and Taiwanese and Japanese stock gains.
The Taiwan Weighted Index closed 4.94% up at 41,664.7, marking it largest one-day gain since 31 July.
The index was powered by gains in tech heavyweights Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Hon Hai Precision Industry — also known as Foxconn.
South Korea's Kospi fell 0.81% after a choppy session to end at 5,018.85, while the small-cap Kosdaq slipped 0.82% to 638.97.
Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 2.33% higher at 58,775.5, and the broad-based Topix saw a larger increase of 2.97% to 3,818.16.
Mainland China's CSI 300 rose marginally to 4,056.11, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was flat in its last hour of trade.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.1% to 9,029.7.
Crédit Agricole has proposed merging its Italian operation with Banco BPM in a deal that would create Italy's third-largest banking group.
The French lender said in a statement Monday that the "friendly proposal" to engage its Italian peer in merger discussions is a "natural extension" of the long-term partnership between the pair.
Under the deal, Crédit Agricole would increase its current 29.6% stake in Banco BPM to approximately 45% of the new combined entity.
The proposal offers Banco BPM shareholders a 20% premium to the relative valuation of the businesses, based on estimated 2027 price-to-earnings multiples, and a 1 billion euro ($1.12 billion) special dividend, according to Crédit Agricole's announcement.
The Paris-headquartered bank said the deal — which has been submitted to Banco BPM's board of directors for evaluation — could deliver 800 million in annual synergies, with about 24% 2027 earnings-per-share accretion expected.
"This strategic project would create Italy's third-largest banking group, serving 6.5 million customers through more than 2,300 branches, by combining a strong local presence, financial strength, and business expertise," Crédit Agricole added.
European bourses are heading for a weak open, according to IG futures data. France's CAC 40 , Germany's DAX and Italy's FTSE MIB were all seen slipping, though the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was last seen slightly higher.
It follows last week's post-midterms markets rollercoaster, with strong gains on Nov. 4 followed by a selloff on Nov. 5 and 6. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index ended the week 0.24% higher.
UniCredit 's third-quarter net profit rose by a record 24% year-on-year to 3.3 billion euros ($3.68 billion), beating consensus estimates of 2.78 billion euros, as revenues reached 6.9 billion euros, up 12% year-on-year.
The Italian bank, which is set to take control of German lender Commerzbank , also hiked its full-year profit guidance to full-year profit guidance to "well above" 11.5 billion euros, from more than 11 billion euros.

articles.title_orig: Rubio says Iranians making ‘outrageous and ridiculous’ demands in negotiations
articles.title_zh: Rubio says Iranians making ‘outrageous and ridiculous’ demands in negotiations
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Iran of "outrageous and ridiculous" demands as efforts to reach a lasting resolution in the Middle East war appeared stalled.
Speaking with reporters in Florida on Sunday evening before traveling to Paris for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting, Rubio indicated the two sides remain far apart on negotiations, after Tehran proposed shortening the timetable for restarting talks from seven days to two.
Rubio said President Donald Trump would prefer to solve "this and every problem diplomatically," but added that "sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately."
Energy prices moved lower on Monday morning after President Trump said Sunday that further strikes were "highly unlikely" if negotiations progressed toward a strong agreement.
Brent crude , the international price benchmark, was down 0.75% at $97.58 per barrel by 5:25 a.m. ET. Meanwhile, U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery were trading 0.42% lower at $90.45.
Trump said in a CNN interview prior to Rubio's comments that a resumption of hostilities in the more than eight-month-long conflict was unlikely, provided that talks to constrain Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz can progress.
"I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said. "Right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable but, in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic."
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday that Tehran wants U.S. sanctions lifted and the war ended on all fronts before negotiations begin.

articles.title_orig: Passenger trains crash in Egypt, killing 7 and injuring 125, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Passenger trains crash in Egypt, killing 7 and injuring 125, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.
The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.
Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise.
The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients.
Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries.
The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing aid and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene.
The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed.
The first train involved in the crash was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks.
Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two.
Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. The railway authority has not said how long it expects this to take.
The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.
In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.
Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.
There were calls in Egypt on Sunday for the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster.
Foreign leaders and dignitaries have shared condolences and support for the victims.
Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished those hurt a speedy recovery.
Turkey's ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families, and the Egyptian people.

articles.title_orig: China Producer Inflation Accelerates as Consumer Prices Cool
articles.title_zh: China Producer Inflation Accelerates as Consumer Prices Cool
articles.content_orig:
Producer prices in China grew at the fastest rate since June 2022, accelerating for the third month in a row.
The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters. The increase was driven by a sharp rise in prices in the mining and raw materials industries.
The increase was driven by very strong external demand, Zhang Zhiwei, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, told CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ."
Consumer inflation in China slowed to 0.7% in October, its first deceleration after two straight months of increases.
The figure missed expectations of a 0.8% rise from economists polled by Reuters, and was lower than the 0.9% seen in September.
Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, came in at 0.8%, down from the 1% seen in the month before.
The rise in consumer prices were still held up by prices of gasoline, which was the largest contributor to the increase in prices, but this was offset by a sharper than expected fall in food prices, according to Dong Lijuan, chief statistician of the urban division at China's National Bureau of Statistics.
The Chinese economy has shown some signs of expansion recently. It grew faster than expected in the third quarter, and September saw a sharp beat in retail sales.
The mainland Chinese CSI 300 index gained 0.56% after the data release.
Pinpoint's Zhang said that domestic demand has been rather weak due to the property market, and this is a key reason why inflation is not picking up in China "There's no clear sign of stabilization [in that sector] yet," he said, adding this was weighing on the household consumer confidence and local government revenue.
"So the the overall economic momentum has been weak and hasn't really seen [a] clear sign of recovery," Zhang explained.
